items.front_excerpt: Ternary Logic and Logic with Independence This note explores a possible relationship between a computational ternary logic and a richer logic that explicitly represents independence. Computational ternary logic Use three values: T: the statement has a verified proof. F: the negation has a verified proof. U: neither has been established. The value U represents only the current state of knowledge; it does not imply mathematical independence. Logic with independence A richer logic distinguishes: T: provable. F: refutable.
